# Enable Cloud Browsing

## Goal

Complete the basic **machine -> browser instance -> user Cloud Browser** flow so users can open a remote browser from the Sa2web frontend.

Cloud Browsing creates separate remote browser profiles for each access environment based on the user, proxy, and isolated network.

For example, after User A accesses and logs in to a website through Cloud Browsing, User B will not inherit User A’s login state when accessing the same website. Their cookies, sessions, and other browser data remain isolated from each other.

Likewise, even for the same user, if User A accesses the same website through Proxy A and Proxy B, the two access environments will use separate browser profiles. Their cookies, sessions, and other browser data remain isolated and are not shared between the two environments.

## Add a Machine

Go to:

```text
Browser Management > Machine Management
```

Click **Add Machine** and fill in:

| Field | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| IP address | The private IP of the current Sa2web deployment server |
| Port | Default `7000` |

After saving, return to the machine list and confirm that the machine status is normal, as shown in @fig-add-machine.

![Sa2web add machine](/images/add-machine.png){#fig-add-machine}

## Add a Browser

Go to:

```text
Browser Management > Browser List
```

Click **Add Navigator**, as shown in @fig-add-browser, and fill in:

| Field | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Machine | Select the machine you just added |
| Browser version | Use the built-in browser version |
| Browser ID | Enter an easy-to-recognize ID, such as `chrome100` |

Choose the network mode based on your scenario:

| Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| Host Network | Uses the server's local network. HTTP/SOCKS5 proxies can be configured. Suitable for general access scenarios |
| Isolated Network | Creates an independent network environment for this browser. DNS, UDP, WebRTC, and other traffic are taken over. Suitable for scenarios with stronger network isolation requirements |

If you choose **Isolated Network**, you need to configure a network proxy for the current browser. Proxies configured elsewhere in the system, such as site-level proxies, will be chained on top of this network proxy.

After saving, click to start the browser. When the status becomes `Running`, the browser instance can be scheduled, as shown in @fig-browser-status.

![Sa2web add browser](/images/add-browser.png){#fig-add-browser}

![Sa2web browser status](/images/browser-status.png){#fig-browser-status}

## Configure the Browser

In the browser list, click the "![](/images/wrench.png){width=20px}" button to open the browser configuration page.

Common settings include:

- Kernel version.
- Operating system.
- Browser brand.
- Browser version.
- Mobile phone model.
- Time zone.
- Language.

![Sa2web browser configuration](/images/browser-config.png){#fig-browser-config}

For more complete configuration details, see the browser instance configuration section in @sec-sites-inner-sites-config, "Site and Inner Site Configuration".

## Create and Authorize a Group

Go to:

```text
Group Management
```

Add a new group, such as `demo`, as shown in @fig-group-management. Then open the user configuration for the group and add the test user to it. During the first test, you may only have the `system` user, so add it to the group and save, as shown in @fig-group-users.

![Sa2web group management](/images/group-management.png){#fig-group-management}

![Sa2web group users](/images/group-users.png){#fig-group-users}

Next, open **Privileges** and select the features required by the `demo` group. For minimum validation, select at least **Cloud Browser** and save, as shown in @fig-group-privileges.

If you used an isolated network earlier, also go to:

```text
Cloud Browser Isolated Networks
```

Select the browser you just created, such as `chrome100`, and save, as shown in @fig-group-privileges-isolated.

![Sa2web group privileges](/images/group-privileges.png){#fig-group-privileges}

![Sa2web isolated network authorization](/images/group-privileges-isolated.png){#fig-group-privileges-isolated}

## Verify the User Frontend

Open the user frontend:

```text
https://<APP_DOMAIN>/
```

You can also open the login page directly:

```text
https://<APP_DOMAIN>/app/login
```

Log in as an authorized user. After entering the frontend, you will see a search and URL input box near the top center of the page, with proxy and network selectors nearby.

If you configured an isolated network, first choose the authorized browser in the network dropdown, such as `chrome100`. Then enter a keyword or URL in the input box:

```text
demo
https://www.sa2web.com
```

If a new tab opens and web browsing works normally, Cloud Browser is available, as shown in @fig-cloud-browser.

![Sa2web Cloud Browser](/images/cloud-browser.png){#fig-cloud-browser}

## Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] The machine has been added with port `7000`.
- [ ] The browser has been added and is in `Running` state.
- [ ] The user has been added to the correct group.
- [ ] The group has been authorized for **Cloud Browser**.
- [ ] If using an isolated network, the group has been authorized for the corresponding browser.
- [ ] The user frontend can open Cloud Browser.
- [ ] The remote browser can access the test page.
